title: Clopen pro-etale component decomposition and K-injective insertion
statement:
Let $X,V$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $q:V\to X$ be a scheme morphism, and let $s:X\hookrightarrow V$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with closed image and $qs=1_X$. Put $Z=V\setminus s(X)$ with open inclusion $t:Z\hookrightarrow V$. For a finite commutative ring $A$, use module sheaves over the constant coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Restriction gives an exact equivalence
$$\operatorname{Mod}(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\times\operatorname{Mod}(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A),\qquad F\mapsto(s^*F,t^*F),$$
under which extension by zero $s_!$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero] is the insertion $M\mapsto(M,0)$. The induced equivalence on unbounded cochain complexes carries acyclic complexes and chain homotopies componentwise. In particular, if $I$ is K-injective on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], then $s_!I$ is K-injective on $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The ordinary direct image of [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] has a natural isomorphism $q_*s_!M\cong M$ for every module sheaf $M$: on each site object $W\to X$ its map is restriction of sections on $V\times_XW$ to the component $s(X)\times_XW\cong W$. This isomorphism extends termwise to complexes and commutes with chain maps and homotopies.
